rows.acip: RNAL 'BYOR SPYOD PA BA RNAMS KYIS GNAS GYUR PA'I SEMS KYI DAG PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA CIG, SO SO RANG GIS RIG PA'I SPYOD YUL DU GRUB PA KHAS BLANGS PA BKAG PA'I TSE,
rows.wylie: rnal 'byor spyod pa ba rnams kyis gnas gyur pa'i sems kyi dag pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa cig, so so rang gis rig pa'i spyod yul du grub pa khas blangs pa bkag pa'i tshe
rows.english: Let's consider the point at which we deny the position of those who belong to the school of deep practice, as they assert an adventitious purity of the mind which could exist through some nature of its own, and which could serve as the sphere of activity for the state of mind which could perceive itself, in the same moment that it perceives other objects.
rows.raw: {"course": "ILL", "acip": "RNAL 'BYOR SPYOD PA BA RNAMS KYIS GNAS GYUR PA'I SEMS KYI DAG PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA CIG, SO SO RANG GIS RIG PA'I SPYOD YUL DU GRUB PA KHAS BLANGS PA BKAG PA'I TSE,", "wylie": "rnal 'byor spyod pa ba rnams kyis gnas gyur pa'i sems kyi dag pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa cig, so so rang gis rig pa'i spyod yul du grub pa khas blangs pa bkag pa'i tshe", "english": "Let's consider the point at which we deny the position of those who belong to the school of deep practice, as they assert an adventitious purity of the mind which could exist through some nature of its own, and which could serve as the sphere of activity for the state of mind which could perceive itself, in the same moment that it perceives other objects."}

rows.acip: THOG MAR 'JIG RTEN KHO NAS KHAS BLANGS PA YIN TE, DE'I PHYIR GANG GIS KHAS BLANGS PA DE KHO NA LA LTOS NAS SEL BAR NUS PAS NA BSAL BAR 'OS PA YIN TE, GZHAN DBU MA PA LA LTOS NAS NI MA YIN NO ZHES BSHAD PA
rows.wylie: thog mar 'jig rten kho nas khas blangs pa yin te, de'i phyir gang gis khas blangs pa de kho na la ltos nas sel bar nus pas na bsal bar 'os pa yin te, gzhan dbu ma pa la ltos nas ni ma yin no zhes bshad pa
rows.english: What this is saying is that, to start off, things are accepted only by the world. As such, when we are denying a certain idea we can only do so dependent upon what someone has accepted as the case; this then becomes something worthy of denial. It is not though that we are taking some kind of position relative to what those of the Middle Way are asserting.

rows.acip: MU STEGS CAN RNAMS KYI GZHUNG LUGS RE RE LAS BDAG MI 'DRA BA GANG ZHIG SMRAS PA DE NI, DE DAG GIS JI LTAR BTAGS PA DE LTAR GYUR PA STE DE KHO NA NYID DU YOD PA MIN STE, SKYE BA DANG BRAL PA STE MA SKYES PA'I PHYIR ZHES PA'I RTAGS NI MU STEGS RANG GI RJES SU DPAG PA STE KHAS BLANGS PA'O,,
rows.wylie: mu stegs can rnams kyi gzhung lugs re re las bdag mi 'dra ba gang zhig smras pa de ni, de dag gis ji ltar btags pa de ltar gyur pa ste de kho na nyid du yod pa min ste, skye ba dang bral pa ste ma skyes pa'i phyir zhes pa'i rtags ni mu stegs rang gi rjes su dpag pa ste khas blangs pa'o
rows.english: The various scriptural traditions within the River Schools thus then present different versions of the self. But it is not the case that what they impute here is the way things actually are: it is not the case that it is indeed reality. The reasoning which says that “things are devoid of arising, because they cannot have arisen” is just the River Schools expressing their own process of deduction: their own position.

rows.acip: DE'I DUS KYI BDAG KYANG LUS LTAR ZHIG PAS, DA LTA MED PA'I PHYIR DANG, TSE 'DIR SNGAR GYI BDAG LAS RANG BZHIN GYIS THA DAD PA'I BDAG GZHAN SKYES PAR KHAS BLANGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
rows.wylie: de'i dus kyi bdag kyang lus ltar zhig pas, da lta med pa'i phyir dang, tshe 'dir sngar gyi bdag las rang bzhin gyis tha dad pa'i bdag gzhan skyes par khas blangs pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: And that's because you have taken the position that the self that I had in those days gone by would have ended just as the body did—and could no longer exist at present. And that means you are saying that yet another self would have taken birth here in this life: one which was essentially separate from that previous self.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR SA MYUG SOGS LA, RTEN 'BREL RKYEN NYID 'DI PA TZAM KHAS BLANGS PA LTAR, SHING RTA YANG RANG GI YAN LAG LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PAR KHAS BLANGS PA'I PHYIR, KHO BO CAG GI PHYOGS LA SHING RTA 'ON CIG CES PA SOGS KYI 'JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD MI RUNG BAR MI 'GYUR LA,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir sa myug sogs la, rten 'brel rkyen nyid 'di pa tsam khas blangs pa ltar, shing rta yang rang gi yan lag la brten nas btags par khas blangs pa'i phyir, kho bo cag gi phyogs la shing rta 'on cig ces pa sogs kyi 'jig rten gyi tha snyad mi rung bar mi 'gyur la
rows.english: As such, when we're talking about things like seeds & sprouts, the view that we have accepted is this kind of dependent interconnection, this pure sort of causality. Just so, what we say is that wagons as well are things that are labeled, in dependence upon their component parts. Thus it is not the case that, according to our position, there is any possibility that the parlance of the world—“Bring that wagon” and so forth—could ever be somehow inappropriate.

rows.acip: PHA ROL POS RGYU 'BRAS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR KHAS BLANGS LA, RANG GIS RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA'I SGYU MA BZHIN DU KHAS BLANGS PA BKOD DO,,
rows.wylie: pha rol pos rgyu 'bras rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par khas blangs la, rang gis rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa'i sgyu ma bzhin du khas blangs pa bkod do
rows.english: And that is that when our opponent has accepted cause & effect that could exist by definition, we present to them our position, that these are things that cannot exist by themselves, through some kind of self-nature; but are, rather, similar to an illusion.

rows.acip: TSIG GSAL GYI STONG THUN DU 'DIR SKYE BA BKAG PA BSGRUB BYA'I CHOS SU 'DOD PA'I TSE DE KHO NAR RTEN CHOS CAN PHYIN CI LOG TZAM GYI BDAG GI DNGOS PO RNYED PA NYAMS PAR 'GYUR BAR RTOG GE PA 'DIS RANG NYID KYIS KHAS BLANGS PA YIN NO ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
rows.wylie: tshig gsal gyi stong thun du 'dir skye ba bkag pa bsgrub bya'i chos su 'dod pa'i tshe de kho nar rten chos can phyin ci log tsam gyi bdag gi dngos po rnyed pa nyams par 'gyur bar rtog ge pa 'dis rang nyid kyis khas blangs pa yin no zhes gsungs so
rows.english: He expresses this point in his interlude on emptiness known as A Clarification of the Verses: When we take the position here that denying the growth of things is the quality we seek to prove, then this logician has-on his own accord-accepted precisely, with nothing more than this, that the idea that the basis of the quality (the subject under consideration) can be perceived to be a self-existing entity, and thus simply mistaken, has been compromised.

rows.english: Well, if you look at it that way, then maybe we should say that the Numerists are Buddhists! Why do you say that? Because they take the position that parts of a person have no self-nature.

rows.wylie: rigs pa ltar snang 'di lta bu la brten nas dbu ma pa la khas len med ces zer na kho bos kyang rnam rig pa la khas lan med ces smra bar bya'o, ,des dngos po rang mtshan khas blangs pas so zhe na
rows.english: One may make this claim: People have used faulty logic like that to make the claim that followers of the Middle Way take no position at all; our reply is to assert that it is the Mentalists who take no position. And that's because they agree to the idea that functional things have an existence in & of themselves.

rows.acip: THA SNYAD KYI SKABS SU GZHAN NGO'AM 'KHRUL NGO ZHES TSIG TU MA BRJOD PAR RNAM GZHAG MI SHES PA DE DAG GIS NI BDEN PA GNYIS PO TSA REG DANG GRANG REG BZHIN DU KHAS BLANGS PA
rows.wylie: tha snyad kyi skabs su gzhan ngo'am 'khrul ngo zhes tshig tu ma brjod par rnam gzhag mi shes pa de dag gis ni bden pa gnyis po tsha reg dang grang reg bzhin du khas blangs pa
rows.english: These people don't understand the usage where-when we are referring to the conventional-we add the wording "to the perceptions of these others," or "to perceptions which are mistaken"; rather, they take the position that the two realities are opposed, like the touch of something very hot and the touch of something very cold.

rows.acip: THABS DANG THABS BYUNG DU BZHAG MI NUS SHING, DON DAM GYI RNAM GZHAG MI NUS TE, DON DAM GYI RNAM GZHAG BYED NA KUN RDZOB YOD PA MA YIN PAR MO GSHAM GYI BU BZHIN DU KHAS BLANGS PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: thabs dang thabs byung du bzhag mi nus shing, don dam gyi rnam gzhag mi nus te, don dam gyi rnam gzhag byed na kun rdzob yod pa ma yin par mo gsham gyi bu bzhin du khas blangs pa'i phyir
rows.english: As such, they are unable to lay out the concepts of method and that which results from employing the method; which means they are unable then to describe what is ultimate. They would say that-if you can make a presentation of the ultimate-then necessarily the deceptive could not exist at all; they would take the position that deceptive reality would be like that child of a barren woman.

rows.acip: 'DIR DAM BCA' MED PAR BSHAD PA DANG, RTZA SHER MTHA' BZHI 'GOG PA'I DAM BCA' KHAS BLANGS PA JI LTAR ZHE NA,

rows.english: And then next someone may come and ask- How can you reconcile the fact that here in this text you are presenting an explanation which says that these thinkers take no position at all; while you still assert that you accept the position taken by The Arya himself in Wisdom, as he denies the four extremes?

rows.acip: DANG PO LA, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA KHAS BLANGS PAS GZHAN SDE LAS RANG GI RTZA BA'I GRUB MTHA' DANG 'GAL BA MED PAR THAL BA, RANG SDES KHAS LEN PA CHES MI RIGS PA DANG, DE'I 'THAD PA'O,,
rows.wylie: dang po la, rang bzhin gyis grub pa khas blangs pas gzhan sde las rang gi rtsa ba'i grub mtha' dang 'gal ba med par thal ba, rang sdes khas len pa ches mi rigs pa dang, de'i 'thad pa'o
rows.english: The presentation itself has three sections: (1) how it is that people's own most basic position in no way contradicts that of the others, given that they accept the idea that things exist through some nature of their own; (2) how it is that it would be incorrect in the extreme for our own groups to accept that idea; and (3) why this idea is itself quite correct.
